description:
Exiled Sector

Still sane, exile?

Designed to be an overhaul of the simple hullmod system based on the infamous Path of Exile skill tree, Exiled Sector is a Starsector mod that gives every ship in your fleet its own skill tree.

Manual download

|

Source (GitHub)

Features

Open the refit screen and click the skill tree button on any of your ships. There's a whole new sector in there:

Spoiler[close]

Every ship gets its own tree, with over 300 nodes.Some nodes are travel nodes that let you choose between several options.

Spoiler[close]

Nodes start out costing OP: 1 for frigates, 2 for destroyers, 3 for cruisers and 4 for capitals. Ships also earn XP in combat and level up, and every level lets you take a node for free. Veteran ships get their ordnance points back. The crew gets nothing, as is tradition.Some nodes are hidden until you unlock them.

Spoiler[close]

Plenty of nodes have effects you won't find anywhere in vanilla.Beams can split between targets, so your Tachyon Lance can finally disappoint several enemies at once.

Spoiler

[close]

Each faction has its own corner of the tree with thematic nodes. For example, your ship's main goal can be to blow up, and act like it don't know nobody.

Spoiler

[close]

Requirements

Starsector 0.98a-RC8LazyLibMagicLibLunaLib

Optional:

Console Commands adds ExiledSectorGrantFleetXp [amount].A healthy disregard for vanilla balance.

Compatibility

Warning:

Exiled Sector adds permanent hull mods to the ships in your fleet. It is not safe to remove after being used.

It should be safe to add to an existing save.

Nodes that copy a vanilla hull mod also place the real hull mod on the ship as a phantom: it costs no OP and does nothing itself, but other mods that check for that hull mod see it. That should make most mods work with the tree's nodes without needing dedicated support.

These mods have dedicated compatibility. The version listed is the one I last tested against. Newer versions usually work; if one doesn't, starsector.log says so at startup and lists anything Exiled Sector can no longer find.

Mod

Tested version

What Exiled Sector does with it

Second-in-Command

2.0.0Its skills see the hull mods your nodes stand in for, and Reconfiguration waives the Converted Hangar penalties.Lost Sector0.6.2dThe Kesteven and Frozen Heart areas of the tree appear, and Augmented Systems hulls get the same bonuses from those nodes as from the hull mods.

MagicLib

1.5.6Required. A hull mod that tries to strip one of your nodes' hull mods through MagicLib is removed instead.

Some weapons from other mods misbehave (often hilariously) when their beams are split or their shots are chained. These are listed in:

data/config/exiledSector/split_beam_effect_blocklist.csvdata/config/exiledSector/energy_chain_blocklist.csv

Both files are merged across mods, so other mods can opt their own weapons out (or you can opt them back in, at your own risk).

Languages

Exiled Sector is available in English and Simplified Chinese. By default it follows the game's language, so a Chinese-localised Starsector shows the skill tree in Chinese automatically. You can also pick a language in the LunaLib settings; the change takes effect after a restart.

The skill tree screen always shows the chosen language, using a bundled Noto Sans SC font. Text the game draws itself (settings, dialogs, the codex) stays in English unless the game can display Chinese characters.

The Chinese translation is a first draft awaiting review by a native speaker. To add another language, see the

localisation guide

.

FAQ

How do I earn and spend points?

SpoilerOpen a ship's refit screen and click the

Skill Tree

button under the hull mods, or press

K

.

The first time you open a ship's tree you choose where it starts: Low Tech, Midline or High Tech. The starting node is free. Whenever it is the only node allocated, you can click it again to choose a different start. The other two can still be reached later like any other node.

Every node costs the ship's unused ordnance points: 1 for frigates, 2 for destroyers, 3 for cruisers and 4 for capitals. A node can only be allocated next to one you already have. Node tooltips show only what a node does. Press

F1

while hovering one to also see its restrictions, such as the hull mods and nodes it is mutually exclusive with.

After every engagement, each ship in your fleet gains XP equal to the deployment points of the enemy ships destroyed or disabled, whether it deployed or not. Harder fights pay more: the same battle difficulty bonus vanilla shows before combat ("Additional XP due to overall battle difficulty") multiplies it, up to 6×. Easier fights never reduce it. You get half as much if you lose.

Each level makes your most recently bought node free and refunds its OP. If every node you have is already free, the level is banked, and your next node costs nothing. The first level takes 60 XP, each level after that takes 13% more until level 25, and ships cap at level 50.

Click an allocated node to remove it. OP-paid nodes refund their OP, and free nodes return their free allocation. You can't remove a node that other nodes depend on to connect back to your starting point, and you can't remove the starting point itself.

Ctrl+Shift+click an allocated node to remove it along with every node that depends on it, starting with the farthest. Doing this on your starting point clears the whole tree and lets you choose a new start. For now it does nothing if any of those nodes has its own removal condition (currently any node that adds fighter bays).

For multi-choice nodes, click to open a dropdown so you can pick an option. Ctrl+click repeats your last choice.

Each ship can have a max of 60 nodes.

Every number in this section can be changed in LunaLib settings.

[close]

What's the difference between "increases" and "more"?

SpoilerThey're two different kinds of modifier, and they stack very differently. If you've played Path of Exile, it's a similar convention.

Starsector calculates a stat like this:

Code

modified = base + base * percentMod / 100 + flatMod;
modified *= mult;

Tooltip wording

added together

first, including those from vanilla hullmods and skills."

added together

first (10% more + 10% more = 20% more; 15% more + 30% less = 15% less), and never go past 100% less. They still multiply with multipliers from vanilla hullmods and skills.

For example, with a base of 1000 flux capacity:

Two "Increases flux capacity by 10%" nodes give 1000 × (1 + 0.10 + 0.10) = 1200.Two "10% more flux capacity" nodes give 1000 × (1 + 0.10 + 0.10) = 1200, applied after everything else."Increases by 15%", "Increases by 600", a +10% hullmod and "20% more" together give (1000 + 250 + 600) × 1.2 = 2220.

Numbers are green when they help your ship and orange when they hurt it.

How do NPC fleets get skill trees?

SpoilerEvery fleet can have trees, in every faction, including your own faction's fleets and your allies. Stations don't get them.

Ships with officers and the flagship always get a tree. Each other ship has a 30% chance. Civilian and mothballed ships are left out. The roll is fixed per ship, so reloading a save won't reroll it.

The number of nodes depends on your character level when the fleet is first spawned:

Your level

Nodes

11–2511–131013–2815+16–42

Every NPC captain reads their ship's specs and makes a plan. The plan is usually sensible and occasionally baffling.

They start from the root that matches their hull's design type (Low Tech, Midline or High Tech), or from wherever their academy, priest or AI author happened to teach. Their first job is replacing refit hullmods the tree offers a node for. The OP that frees up buys extra nodes, but if the node is out of reach they keep the hullmod. Built-in hullmods and S-mods are never touched.

Faction captains owe their volume a visit. Ships from a faction with its own volume cross vast expanses to take one notable or keystone there, if they can afford the trip.

After that it's down to taste. A captain picks notables and keystones that suit their weapons, fighters, shields or phase cloak, armour and built-in hullmods, but their choices are often like the sector: random and brutal. aiDescription: Overhauls the hullmod system by giving each ship a unique skill tree with over 300 nodes. Ships earn XP in combat to unlock nodes for free, while others cost ordnance points. The system includes faction-specific areas, hidden nodes, and compatibility with other mods through phantom hullmods.

changelog.0.6.0:
New features
Added a hyperspace map. If you keep scrolling out past the minimum zoom, the view glides out to a map of every region's main star.
Added smart respec. Ctrl+Shift+click an allocated node to remove it and every node that depends on it, one at a time at auto-allocate's pace, farthest first, with the clicked node last. Doing this on the starting point clears the tree and returns you to the starting point choice. A click or Escape cancels a respec in progress. It does nothing if any node it would remove has its own removal condition.
The starting root can now be chosen again. While it is the only allocated node, click it to undo the choice.
Added Lost Sector themed areas to the skill tree (with permission). These new areas are optional, with direct ports of some Kesteven hullmods and some thematic designs of my own.
Auto shows it only when Lost Sector is installed, and On and Off in Lunalib override that.
Switching an area off removes its nodes from every ship and refunds their OP, banked allocations and item costs. The change applies on the next save load.

The refit screen has a new Skill Tree button (hotkey K) one slot below Build In. With Ship Mastery System installed, it sits directly under the Mastery button. This replaces the old button to open the skill tree.
The Exiled Sector Skill Tree hull mod is now visible in the refit screen.
Hovering it lists an aggregate of every bonus from the ship's allocated nodes, up to 25 lines plus a count of the rest.
Clicking its icon opens the skill tree.

Nodes that copy a vanilla hull mod now place the real hull mod on the ship as a phantom.
The phantom is permanent, costs 0 OP and does nothing by itself, but other mods that check for that hull mod see it.
High Resolution Sensors and Phase Field are the exceptions.
Phantoms are hidden from the refit screen's installed hull mod lists and from ships' Codex related entries, and their tooltip names the node that provides them. They still appear as hullmods in some areas.

Multipliers from the skill tree ("% more / % less") now add together instead of compounding.
For example, 2% + 2% more is now 4% more, and 15% more plus 30% less is 15% less. The total never goes past 100% less.
Temporary nodes still apply their own multiplier that can compound.
The X panel summary adds them the same way and hides multipliers that cancel out.

Added drastically improved NPC fleet generation logic, introducing themed randomness to all NPC fleets.
Node tooltips now show only the description, effects and temporary duration.
Press F1 in the skill tree to show or hide the rest: mutual exclusivity, hull requirements, hull sizes, item cost, deallocation warnings and the free-node note.

Compatibility
Lost Sector (tested with 0.6.2d) is optional.
With it installed, the Kesteven and Frozen Heart areas appear, controlled by the Optional Areas setting.
Kesteven nodes place Lost Sector's own hull mods as phantoms.
On hulls with Augmented Systems, these nodes give the same extra bonuses as Lost Sector's hull mods. Volatile Flux Injector's high-flux penalties are halved, and Inertial Supercharger also raises projectile speed by its damage bonus.

Second-in-Command changes:
It now sees the real Shield Shunt and Safety Overrides hull mods through their phantoms, so its own Redistribution and Enhanced Overrides bonuses apply.
The tree's "counts as" stand-in lines are gone.
It also sees Militarized Subsystems as installed.

MagicLib: when another hull mod tries to strip one of a node's phantom hull mods through MagicLib, that hull mod is removed instead.
Ship Mastery System and other mods that check for Safety Overrides now see it on ships with the node.
The skill tree hull mod now applies after every other hull mod, including D-mods and Second-in-Command's controller, so crew-based effects see the final values.
Split-beam and refraction drones now copy marker hull mods from the firing ship.
This makes ET-IX's Dawnstar and Daythorn beams, and the misfire checks of ET-IX and Emergent Threats beams, work on drones.
The list is in data/config/exiledSector/drone_marker_hullmods.csv, which merges across mods.

The beam split and refraction blocklists were re-checked against the new drones.
The Repulser, the energy ball launcher and the Supernova now refract normally, so the refraction blocklist is empty.
Devastator, Whiplash, Limited Ammo, SBE, Fermion Decoupler, Electrolaser Pulse and Destiny Spear beams now split normally.
Six beam effects stay blocked.

At startup, starsector.log gets a self-check line for Lost Sector, Second-in-Command and MagicLib. It says whether each mod is absent, at the tested version, at an untested version, or missing something Exiled Sector relies on.
The mod no longer ships a copy of vanilla's Orbitron 20 bold font, which broke campaign UI text alongside font or localisation mods.

Bug fixes
Fixed Refracting Projectiles crashing combat on some modded projectiles. Refracted shots also no longer appear on the shield they just hit, or break on special projectiles.
Fixed Lion's Gaze split-beam drones staying in battle forever after the firing ship retreated or its wreck was removed.
Fixed a crash on loading a save, caused by the tree changing hull mods during the game's OP-cost calculation.
Fixed Fighter Replacement nodes speeding up fighter replacement rate decay instead of slowing it.
Fixed Phase Anchor's emergency dive trying to trigger on ships without a phase cloak.
Fixed XP not being awarded for auto-resolved pursuits.
Fixed captured NPC ships losing their skill tree when another fight followed straight away.
Fixed two one-way links in the tree. They now unlock from either end.
Choice nodes whose chosen option no longer exists, or is no longer offered, are now removed and refunded on load. A skill type that fails to load no longer changes saves.
Choice nodes are now checked against the restrictions of both the node and the chosen option, everywhere.
Nodes removed from the tree, or from a switched-off area, now also refund their item cost.
Tooltip tables now use the current root's accent colour instead of the colour they were first drawn with.
Raised the limit on ships that can hold paid skill tree nodes at the same time from 1,000 to 10,000.
changelog.0.5.0:
Features
You can now save a ship's skill tree as a named template and load it onto any other ship with the same starting node. A loaded template shows its path as green connectors, and the Auto-allocate button fills it in for you, skipping any nodes that are blocked or cost items.
Ships now earn more XP from harder fights, using the same difficulty rating vanilla shows before combat. It only ever adds XP, the post-battle report tells you how much, and you can adjust its strength and cap in LunaLib.
Improved allocation animations
If a future update removes nodes from the tree, your ships get back the OP and free allocations they spent on them. If a ship's starting root is removed, its tree is reset so you can pick a new one, and it keeps its level, XP and banked allocations. Hopefully this makes skill tree iterations not break your saves.

Bug fixes
Nodes could end up costing no OP. The hidden hull mods that reserve OP for skill nodes leaked until they ran out, and after that new ships reserved nothing.
A giant stretched ship hull could sometimes appear across the skill tree (the HOUND bug).
Skills that add OP to every ship in the fleet only counted toward the flagship's skill tree budget. They now count for every ship.
Nodes allocated on a ship you had just bought could give no bonuses and reserve no OP. Not 100% sure this is fixed yet.
Pressing Escape in the search box closed the whole panel; now it just clears the search.
changelog.0.4.0:
New features
Some nodes are now limited to certain hull sizes, like their vanilla hull mods.
New split notables for things like Expanded Magazines.
Balance changes to several nodes.
Massive improvements to performance.

Bug fixes
Fixed nodes allocated right after choosing a starting point costing no OP.
Missile Autoloader and Neural Interface nodes now work in combat.
Shared Fate and High Scatter Amp now work as described.
Shield Shunt can no longer be taken on phase ships or unshielded ships.
UI and tooltip fixes.
